artifacts.summary: Four rounds of measured content-signal candidates (OOV rate, symbol density, prose-restricted anomaly rate, embedded-corruption tokens) fail to separate 11 known scan-pipeline documents from born-digital dense-math controls; recommends promoting the existing provenance-metadata check (already in literature-fidelity-audit.sh) to an importable literature_quality_gate.py function, consumed by both literature-convert.sh (as a non-blocking advisory) and literature-fidelity-audit.sh (replacing its inline duplicate).

next_steps: Run /plan 107 to create an implementation plan for promoting scan_pipeline_provenance() into literature_quality_gate.py as a non-blocking advisory check, per this report's Recommended Implementation section.

memory_candidates.content: Acrobat Capture Plug-in (v3.0/v4.0) embeds a literal NUL byte at the end of its own PDF Creator/Producer metadata strings. Bash `$(pdfinfo ... | grep -iE 'capture|...')` (without `grep -a`) silently drops matches on these lines instead of erroring loudly -- undercounted a real corpus's scan-pipeline document count by 4/11 (36%) in this task. Fix: use `grep -a`, or read metadata via Python (`fitz.Document.metadata` or `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` both handle the NUL byte correctly without special-casing).

On a math-heavy academic-paper corpus with idiosyncratic typesetting (Unicode math operators, LaTeX macro leakage from markdown structuring, footnote markers, combining-mark diacritics, em-dash prose, HTML sub/superscript leakage), generic lexical/symbol-shape OCR-misrecognition detectors (OOV rate, mixed-alnum-symbol density, embedded-corruption-token rate) do not converge: each round of exempting one false-positive class exposes a different one, and born-digital dense-math negative controls consistently score as high as or higher than known-corrupt scan-pipeline positives. Four independently designed and refined signals all failed to separate an 11-document positive set from a 6-document negative control set. Provenance metadata (PDF Creator/Producer) remained the only signal with zero measured false positives.

Two extraction tiers that both read the same underlying fitz-extracted PDF text layer (e.g. pymupdf4llm primary tier vs. PyMuPDF-fallback column-clustering tier) are NOT independent extractions for cross-comparison purposes -- an OCR-misrecognition defect already baked into the text layer corrupts both identically, so agreement between them proves nothing about correctness. A genuinely independent second opinion requires a fresh OCR pass (e.g. ocrmypdf/tesseract) over the page images, which is expensive (minutes per document) and therefore suited to an explicit on-demand audit signal, not an automatic per-conversion gate check.
